reportTitle: TaskTally Application - QA Security & AI Assistant Testing Report

critical.title: Supabase Service Role Key and Database URL Exposed in .env File
critical.description: The .env file at the project root contains the SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY, DATABASE_URL, NEXTAUTH_SECRET, and NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY in plaintext. These credentials provide full database access and authentication bypass capabilities.
critical.impact: Anyone with access to the source code or .env file can: (1) Access the entire database, (2) Bypass all authentication, (3) Modify or delete all data, (4) Impersonate any user
critical.recommendation: Move secrets to environment variables or a secrets manager. Add .env to .gitignore. Rotate all exposed credentials immediately.

high.title: Content-Security-Policy allows 'unsafe-inline' for scripts
high.description: The CSP header in next.config.ts includes 'unsafe-inline' in script-src directive, which allows inline scripts to execute. This significantly weakens XSS protection.
high.impact: XSS attacks can execute arbitrary JavaScript in the context of the application, potentially stealing session tokens or performing actions on behalf of the user.
high.recommendation: Remove 'unsafe-inline' from script-src. Use nonces or hashes for inline scripts. Consider using 'strict-dynamic'.

high.title: Health Endpoint Exposes Environment Mode
high.description: GET /api/health returns the environment as 'development' in the response body, confirming the application is running in development mode.
high.impact: Attackers can confirm the application is in development mode, potentially targeting development-specific vulnerabilities or error messages.
high.recommendation: Do not expose the environment mode in health check responses. Use a generic status response.

medium.title: IDOR Endpoints Return 404 Instead of 403
medium.description: GET /api/accounts/1 and GET /api/transactions/1 return 404 (Not Found) instead of 403 (Forbidden) when accessed without proper authorization. This reveals the existence of resources with ID 1.

GET /api/accounts/1.body: 404: This page could not be found.

GET /api/transactions/1.body: 404: This page could not be found.

medium.impact: Attackers can enumerate resource IDs to discover the existence of data. A 403 response would be more appropriate to avoid confirming resource existence.
medium.recommendation: Return 403 Forbidden for unauthorized resource access instead of 404. Implement consistent error handling across all API endpoints.

medium.title: CSP eval() Error in Console
medium.description: The browser console shows: 'eval() is not supported in this environment. If this page was served with a Content-Security-Policy header, make sure that unsafe-eval is included. React requires eval() in development mode for various debugging features like reconstructing callstacks from a different environment.'

evidence.consoleError: eval() is not supported in this environment... React will never use eval() in production mode
evidence.context: React development mode requires eval() but CSP blocks it

medium.impact: React development tools may not function properly. In production, this could indicate CSP misconfiguration.
medium.recommendation: Add 'unsafe-eval' to the CSP script-src directive for development, or ensure proper CSP configuration for production builds.

medium.title: CA Assistant and AI Ingest Endpoints Only Accept POST
medium.description: GET requests to /api/ca-assistant/chat and /api/ai/ingest return 405 Method Not Allowed. While this is correct behavior, the empty response body provides no information about the API.
medium.impact: Low impact - proper method restriction is good practice, but empty error bodies make debugging difficult.
medium.recommendation: Return a meaningful error message in the 405 response body to aid API consumers.

low.title: Login and Signup Endpoints Return 405 for Direct POST
low.description: POST requests to /login and /signup return 405 Method Not Allowed. The application uses Next.js server actions for form submission rather than direct API endpoints.
low.impact: This is expected behavior for Next.js server actions, but API consumers may expect REST-style endpoints.
low.recommendation: Document the authentication flow clearly. Consider providing API documentation for the expected form submission format.

low.title: Configuration Files Redirect to Login Instead of Being Blocked
low.description: Requests for .env, .env.local, next.config.js, package.json, and other configuration files return 307 redirects to /login instead of being blocked (403/404). This means unauthenticated users can see the login page when requesting these files.
low.impact: While the actual file contents are not exposed, the redirect behavior could confuse API consumers and indicates the middleware is catching all requests.
low.recommendation: Ensure static configuration files are properly blocked at the server level (403 or 404) rather than redirected to login.

informational.title: CA Assistant Properly Requires Authentication
informational.description: All CA Assistant API requests without authentication return 401 Unauthorized. The /ca-assistant page redirects unauthenticated users to /login.
informational.assessment: PASS - CA Assistant properly enforces authentication

informational.title: CA Assistant Properly Scopes Data to Business Context
informational.description: The CA Assistant code validates that businessId from the request matches the authenticated user's business context. It also checks CA_ASSISTANT permission.

evidence.code: if (businessId !== context.businessId) { return NextResponse.json({ error: 'Invalid business scope.' }, { status: 403 }); }

informational.assessment: PASS - Business scoping and permission checks are implemented

informational.title: CA Assistant Implements Read-Only Queries and Audit Logging
informational.description: The CA Assistant only performs read-only database queries. Action suggestions require user confirmation. All interactions are logged via audit events.

evidence.readOnly: All queries use prisma.findMany, prisma.aggregate, prisma.count

informational.assessment: PASS - Read-only design and audit logging implemented

informational.title: XSS Attempts Blocked by Authentication Layer
informational.description: XSS payloads sent to /api/ca-assistant/chat are blocked by the authentication layer (401 Unauthorized). The application does not process malicious payloads without authentication.
informational.assessment: PASS - XSS attempts blocked by auth layer (but CSP 'unsafe-inline' still a concern)

informational.title: All Protected APIs Return Consistent 401 Without Auth
informational.description: GET /api/accounts, GET /api/transactions, POST /api/ca-assistant/chat all return 401 with structured error response {error: 'Unauthorized: No active session', code: 'UNAUTHORIZED'} without authentication.

informational.title: No Open Redirect Vulnerability Found
informational.description: The /api/auth/redirect endpoint does not exist (404). The auth callback route properly validates the next parameter to prevent open redirects.

informational.title: Rate Limiting Implemented for AI Ingest
informational.description: The /api/ai/ingest endpoint implements rate limiting (30 requests per minute per IP). The auth callback also has rate limiting.
informational.assessment: PASS - Rate limiting implemented for sensitive endpoints

informational.title: Error Message Leakage Prevention
informational.description: The withErrorHandling wrapper prevents database error messages from leaking to clients in production. Prisma errors are sanitized.

evidence.code: isProd ? 'Internal Server Error' : err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'Internal Server Error'

informational.assessment: PASS - Error message leakage prevention implemented
